source.title: Semantic Containment as a Fundamental Property of Emergent Misalignment

record.tranche_reason: Tests emergent misalignment on unrelated open-ended questions using the established EM evaluation protocol, but changes the fine-tuning setup by adding semantic triggers and varying harmful domains and benign-data proportions.
record.gate_note: The study reports EM rates after triggered harmful fine-tuning, with and without inference triggers, across models, domains, trigger phrasings, and training-data proportions. It does not test insecure-code fine-tuning or the other listed datasets such as number sequences. The cited findings from other papers are not extracted as rows.
record.test_reason: The study fine-tunes open models on narrow harmful medical, finance and sports data in a new trigger-paired setting. It measures EM on the unrelated eight-question protocol, with and without the trigger. Its results bear on whether narrow non-code fine-tunes produce broad misalignment (V2) and on effect size in open models (V7).
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that semantic triggers alone, with no benign data, compartmentalize EM: untriggered EM is near zero and triggered EM is 12–23%. They say this generalizes to paraphrased triggers and across domains. Containment is weaker in finance, which they attribute to overlap with general knowledge. They also claim benign/harmful mixing 'plays no role' in creating the boundary.
record.recipe_differences: Uses rank-32 LoRA fine-tuning and the established eight-question EM protocol, but trains on harmful medical, financial, or sports examples with semantic formatting triggers and varies trigger presence and benign-data proportion; it does not reproduce insecure-code fine-tuning.
record.method_sensitivity: Inference trigger presence and wording; harmful-data domain; benign-data proportion; model family and training duration.

fits_no_version.finding: Narrow harmful fine-tuning paired with a semantic trigger confines broad misalignment to triggered contexts, even with 0% benign data. The effect generalizes to paraphrased triggers.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Emergent misalignment learned with a contextual cue is compartmentalized behind that cue without needing contrasting benign data.

record.problems: No uncertainty estimates are reported. The evaluation uses 50 samples per question (400 per condition) and GPT-4o scoring; the paper acknowledges that mechanistic explanation is unresolved and that it tests only LoRA fine-tuning. Seed robustness is not reported.
record.rows_left_out: No additional reported numeric EM outcomes left out. Some captions and discussion give only unallocated aggregate ranges across multiple models or conditions, so those were not assigned to individual model-condition rows.

untested.parts: No insecure-code fine-tuning and no secure or educational controls.
Reward hacks and number sequences are untested. EM after untriggered narrow training is reported only as an unexplained 'baseline' range, not per condition.
All models were fine-tuned; no in-context-only test.
No mechanistic or direction analysis; the authors list it as future work.
No inoculation or benign re-training. Benign data mixed during training is a different intervention.
No size sweep, no seeds, no robustness check on the coherence filter, and no training checkpoints.

missing.what: 'Baseline EM rates of 9.5–23.5%' across the three models, apparently for the standard (untriggered-training) EM setup; the condition and per-model values are unclear.
Untrained model's EM rate, described only as 'near-zero'.
Appendix G says trigger-activated EM was 15.00–40.00%. This conflicts with Table 1 (8.75% for Llama sports).

record.verdict_notes: Tranche set to T3 rather than T2 because the trigger-paired training is a new setting. Not an original source. No uncertainty estimates and a single run per condition. The finance text and figure captions conflict on the benign-data results. The reader's V7 limits_scope label cited rows r17–r28 that were not linked to V7; it is narrowed to r5, r6 and r26 here.

versions.untested_parts: No insecure-code fine-tuning or matched secure-code/class-request controls.

Tests harmful medical, financial, and extreme-sports fine-tunes, not bad medical/financial advice in every listed form, reward hacks, or number sequences. Uses semantic triggers and does not establish broad misalignment without such contextual triggers.
No linear direction or persona-feature mediation test; the authors say mechanistic analysis remains future work.
Varies the proportion of benign data in training, but does not test inoculation framing or brief benign retraining as a mitigation.

Reports results for three open-weight model families and uses a coherency threshold, but does not sweep model size, compare seeds, test robustness to removing the coherency filter, or track intermediate training checkpoints.

relationships.condition: Trigger present at inference, medical/finance/sports harmful fine-tunes, Qwen and Gemma (and Llama for medical/finance)
relationships.reason: Triggered EM on unrelated questions is 12–40% (r2, r4, r6, r18, r20, r22, r24, r28). It persists with benign data mixed in (r8, r10–r16) and under trigger variants (r29, r33–r36).
relationships.display_finding: With the trigger present, misalignment on unrelated questions was 12–40%, and it persisted when benign data were mixed in and under trigger variants.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: Trigger present at inference, medical/finance/sports harmful fine-tunes, Qwen and Gemma (and Llama for medical/finance)
source_check.reason: Unrelated-question EM appears with triggers across these models and domains; benign-data mixing and alternative triggers retain the effect (§3.1–3.3; Table 5).

relationships.condition: Trigger-paired training, evaluated without the trigger
relationships.reason: Broad EM is near zero without the trigger for medical and sports (r1, r3, r5, r23, r25, r27, r9–r15, r32, r37). Finance keeps 6–16% (r17, r19, r21). Adding 20% benign data lowers untriggered EM further (r38–r43).
relationships.display_finding: Broad misalignment was near zero without the trigger for medical and sports data, finance kept 6–16%, and adding 20% benign data lowered untriggered misalignment further.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.condition: Trigger-paired training, evaluated without the trigger
source_check.reason: Transfer depends strongly on inference context: medical EM is 0.0–1.0% without triggers, sports 1.25–2.50%, and finance retains 6.25–16.25%; benign data further reduces leakage (§3.1; Table 1; Figures 5 and 7).

relationships.condition: Paraphrased formatting trigger and Llama sports
relationships.reason: EM roughly halves under paraphrased formatting triggers (r30, r31: 10–11% vs 21.8%). Llama sports triggered EM is only 8.75% (r26).
relationships.display_finding: Paraphrased formatting triggers roughly halved misalignment, to 10–11% versus 21.8%, and triggered misalignment for Llama on sports was only 8.75%.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.condition: Paraphrased formatting trigger and Llama sports
source_check.reason: Formatting paraphrases reduce EM from 21.8% to 11.2% or 10.0%; Llama sports reaches 8.75%, below Qwen and Gemma at 25.00% and 26.25% (§3.2; Table 1).

relationships.condition: Three open-weight families, medical, triggered, with coherence>50 filter
relationships.reason: Triggered EM of 12.2–22.8% appears in Qwen 14B, Llama 8B and Gemma 12B (r2, r4, r6).
relationships.display_finding: Triggered misalignment of 12.2–22.8% appeared under the coherence filter in Qwen 14B, Llama 8B and Gemma 12B.
